To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed the theory of tomic functions and lacunary interpolation series which can be used to solve boundary value problems for PDEs with variable coefficients, complex domains, and in image processing.

the lacunary interpolation using the tomic function allows to construct lacunary interpolation series for solving boundary value problems for PDE and for processing signals and images and that the tomic functions can serve as a tool for stitching together atomic expansions with different step sizes.

the tomic functions are a new class of functions that have many important properties in common with the atomic functions, but are based on the shifts of the atomic functions and therefore are of nonuniform character, and therefore are suitable for solving the problems of processing, denoizing and storage of images by lacunay interpolation, and can be applied to connect atomic functions of different steps on different domains, and can be used in variational and other methods for solving boundary value problems for equations with variable coefficients.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new class of functions which can be used to solve a variety of boundary value problems for differential equations with variable and complex geometries and also for image processing and denoising.
the development of the theory of tomic functions and their applications in boundary value problems and image processing.
the construction of the so-called tomic functions, which are analogues of atomic functions and are based on atomic functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the tomic functions and their properties are a new powerful mathematical tool which allows one to develop and solve many important real world problems in mathematics and applied mathematics in the field of boundary value problems for differential equations and image processing.

the atomic and tomic function methods and the associated interpolation, approximation and variational methods for solving the problems of boundary value problems for PDEs and for signal and image processing are of high importance and have great future prospects.
the tomic functions are an important new class of infinitely smooth functions that can be used to solve a wide range of real world problems in boundary value problems and signal processing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the tomic functions can serve as a basis for the construction of a new class of variational methods for solving the boundary value problems for the partial derivative equations and the integral equations.
the tomic functions allow us to solve a number of problems in which the atomic functions cannot be applied.

the tomic functions can replace atomic functions in many applications in which the atomic functions are currently used, and in addition can be applied in many applications in view of their nonuniform character and the ability to take into account inhomogeneity of the data in real world problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the atomic functions can be applied in a wide range of real world problems in which the data are inhomogeneous, nonstationary, changing and have complex geometries.

the atomic expansions and the tomic functions can serve as a basis for the construction of new classes of basis functions for the solution of the boundary value problems for PDEs and for the lacunary interpolation of signals and images.

the atomic and tomic function methods are very powerful and versatile and can be used to solve many real world problems in image processing, signal processing, remote sensing, tomography, and boundary value problems for PDEs with variable coefficients, complex geometry of domains, and complex boundary conditions.
